output_json.patch_notes: In StaticHandlerImpl.handle(), the single-line normalization `String path = Utils.removeDots(Utils.urlDecode(context.normalisedPath(), false));` was split so that, after url-decoding and before removeDots, backslashes are replaced with forward slashes (`path = path.replace('\\', '/')`) when the decoded path is non-null. This is null-safe (urlDecode may return null, and removeDots already tolerates null). Effect: the malicious request "/%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cwindows%5Cwin.ini" now decodes to "/\..\..\..\..\windows\win.ini", becomes "//../../../../windows/win.ini", and removeDots collapses the leading traversal at the root boundary, yielding "webroot/windows/win.ini" — inside the web root. Added two regression tests to StaticHandlerTest: testCantEscapeWebRootWithEncodedBackslash (encoded-backslash traversal returns 404) and testEncodedBackslashSeparatorsAreNormalized (which distinguishes patched vs unpatched: "/somedir%5C..%5Cotherpage.html" now resolves to /otherpage.html and returns 200, whereas unpatched code left the literal backslash path that does not exist -> 404). Verified: POV run_pov.sh now prints "file path opened by: webroot/windows/win.ini", "RESULT: not vulnerable", exit 1 (was exit 0/VULNERABLE before). Full StaticHandlerTest suite: 58 tests, 0 failures.
output_json.risk_notes: Minimal, focused change confined to the static file handler's request-path normalization; no API or dependency changes. Behavioral note: backslashes in request paths are now treated as path separators for dot-segment removal within StaticHandler. This is the intended hardening and matches how filesystems on Windows interpret such paths; it does not affect legitimate forward-slash URLs. Any (unusual) client relying on literal backslash characters being preserved verbatim in a served filename would now see them normalized to '/', but such paths previously could not be reliably or safely resolved anyway. The regression test command must run with network access (the reactor resolves vertx-web-client from Maven Central); the container's fully-offline mode lacks that artifact.
output_json.summary: Fixed a CWE-022 path traversal in StaticHandlerImpl. Requests whose URLs percent-encode Windows path separators (%5C == '\') bypassed the handler's dot-segment normalization: Utils.removeDots only collapses forward-slash "../" sequences, so a decoded path like "/\..\..\..\..\windows\win.ini" survived intact and escaped the configured web root on platforms where '\' is a separator. The fix normalizes backslashes to forward slashes in StaticHandlerImpl.handle() before removeDots, so backslash-based traversal is collapsed within the web root exactly like forward-slash traversal.
